II. No member of a State Legislative Assembly shall be liable to any proceeding in any court in respect of anything said or any vote given by him/her in the legislature.
Codes
x: Statement I is wrong because the Speaker does not vacate office on dissolution but continues until the new Assembly meets. Statement II (legislative immunity for speech and votes) is correct, so only II is right.

s:
Consider the following statements.

I. The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly shall vacate his/her office if he/she ceases to be a member of the Assembly.

II. Whenever the Legislative Assembly is dissolved, the Speaker shall vacate his/her office immediately.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement II is wrong because the Speaker continues in office after dissolution until just before the new Assembly's first meeting. Statement I is correct, as ceasing to be a member ends the Speaker's office, so only I is right.

s: Which of the following statement(s) is/are NOT one of the powers of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly?
o: He has original vote in all matters
He has no veto except in case of a tie
The Speaker will NOT preside when a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration of the Assembly
x: The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly presides over sessions and ensures orderly conduct of proceedings. However, the Speaker does not possess veto powers except in the case of a tie where he exercises a casting vote. Additionally, when a resolution for his removal is under consideration, he does not preside over the House.

s: If the Speaker of Legislative Assembly of a State wants to resign, he will give his resignation to –
x: According to Article 179(b), if the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of a State wants to resign, he/she will give his resignation to the Deputy Speaker of that State’s Legislative Assembly.

s: If any member of a State Legislature has become subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in Art 192, the question shall be referred to
o: Speaker of the concerned State Assembly
x: Disqualification questions of State legislators are decided by the Governor under Art. 192, acting on the binding opinion of the Election Commission. The ECI only advises; the decision is the Governor's.

s: Who among the following is the final authority to decide any question relating to disqualification of a Member of a House of Legislature of a State?
x: According to Article 192 of the Indian Constitution, if any question arises as to the disqualification of a Member mentioned in clause (1) of Art. 191, the question shall be referred for the decision of the Governor and his decision shall be final but before giving any decision on any such question, the Governor shall obtain the opinion of the Election Commission and shall act according to such opinion.

s: Final decision on question as to disqualification of members of a Legislative Assembly is taken by –
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: According to Article 192, if any question arises as to whether a member of a House of the Legislature of a State has become subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in clause (1) of Article 191, the question shall be referred to the decision of the Governor and his decision shall be final. Before giving any decision on any such question, the Governor shall take the opinion of the Election Commission and shall act according to such opinion.

s: Who decides the disqualification of members of State Legislative Assembly, for matters other than those in the tenth schedule of the Constitution?
x: According to Article 192 of the Constitution, if any member of a state's legislature is disqualified (or ineligible) for any reason, excluding matters related to the tenth schedule, the state governor decides on the matter. However, the decision in this case is made in accordance with the Election Commission's opinion. But, if the disqualification of any member is questioned in the context of the tenth schedule (on the basis of defection), the matter will be decided by the Speaker in the case of the legislative assembly and by the Chairman in the case of the legislative council.

With reference to the Legislative Assembly of a State in India, consider the following statements.

I. The Governor makes a customary address to Members of the House at the commencement of the first session of the year.

II. When a State Legislature does not have a rule on a particular matter, it follows the Lok Sabha rule on that matter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
